subject.title: Workspace symlinks to ~/.openclaw subdirectories are rejected by boundary path check

question: Should fixed workspace bootstrap files be allowed to follow symlink hops into selected `~/.openclaw` sibling directories, and what policy prevents private OpenClaw state from entering startup prompt context?
rationale: The failure is source-reproducible, but the fix changes prompt-authority filesystem boundaries and the prior broad `~/.openclaw` allowance was explicitly rejected as too wide.

options.title: Allow a narrow bootstrap-only exception
options.body: Permit only fixed bootstrap-file symlink hops to approved shared-file locations while rejecting direct arbitrary `~/.openclaw` paths, private state roots, hardlinks, non-regular files, dangling links, and oversized targets.

options.title: Keep strict boundary and improve diagnostics
options.body: Continue blocking external symlink targets but render the condition as boundary-blocked rather than missing so operators can diagnose the setup safely.

options.title: Require explicit trusted-path configuration
options.body: Add or reuse an operator-controlled allowlist before loading external bootstrap targets, accepting the config and upgrade documentation cost.

recommendation.title: Allow a narrow bootstrap-only exception
recommendation.body: Permit only fixed bootstrap-file symlink hops to approved shared-file locations while rejecting direct arbitrary `~/.openclaw` paths, private state roots, hardlinks, non-regular files, dangling links, and oversized targets.

likelyOwner.reason: He owns the open overlapping PR and already stated the next acceptable fix shape for this issue.
